The function <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>t</mi><mo>)</mo></math> that describes this wave equation, if it is travelling in the positive <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math>-direction with a speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> is

solution.text: <math> <mrow> <mi>y</mi> <mfenced close=")" open="(" separators=","> <mrow> <mi>x</mi> <mtext>,</mtext> <mspace width="0.5em"></mspace> <mi>t</mi> </mrow> </mfenced> <mo>=</mo> <mfrac> <mrow> <mi>a</mi> </mrow> <mrow> <msup> <mrow> <mfenced close=")" open="(" separators=","> <mrow> <mi>x</mi> <mo>±</mo> <mi>v</mi><mo>⁡</mo> <mi>t</mi> </mrow> </mfenced> </mrow> <mn>2</mn> </msup> <mo>+</mo> <mi>b</mi> </mrow> </mfrac> </mrow> </math>   is another form of progressive wave equation propagating with a speed v. Negative sign to be taken for propagation along + x-axis and positive sign to be taken for propagation along <math><mrow><mo>-</mo></mrow></math> x-axis.
